FARM.name: Farm
FARM.description: Produces grain that can be milled or sold. Upkeep: 6g/day

MINE.name: Mine
MINE.description: Extracts valuable resources for sale (iron, gold, gems, stone or coal). Upkeep: 15g/day

WORKSHOP.name: Workshop
WORKSHOP.description: Processes raw materials into goods. Upkeep: 10g/day

FISHING_WHARF.name: Fishing Wharf
FISHING_WHARF.description: Send boats to collect fish from nearby waters. Upkeep: 10g/day

BREWERY.name: Brewery
BREWERY.description: Brews beer from grain or distills liquor. Sells well at taverns. Upkeep: 8g/day

TAVERN.name: Tavern
TAVERN.description: A place for drink, gambling, and gossip. Earns gold daily from patrons. Upkeep: 8g/day

GUEST_HOUSE.name: Guest House
GUEST_HOUSE.description: A bed & breakfast: a few rooms and breakfast included. Guests from the town's travellers, shared with its other houses by stars, price and reputation. Hire staff and set prices from its panel. Upkeep: 3g/day

INN.name: Inn
INN.description: A coaching inn: a common room and private rooms, suppers, baths and stabling. Competes with the town's other houses for its travellers. Upkeep: 6g/day

HOTEL.name: Grand Hotel
HOTEL.description: Suites, fine dining, a bathhouse and a valet for the wealthy few. Only a city or capital has the custom. Upkeep: 14g/day

ROADHOUSE.name: Roadhouse
ROADHOUSE.description: A wayside house on an open road between towns: bunks, cheap rooms and a stable yard. Its guests are the road's traffic. Upkeep: 2g/day

GRAIN_MILL.name: Mill
GRAIN_MILL.description: Grinds grain into flour. Built on a river, its water wheel adds +50% output. Build it beside your farm and it mills the harvest automatically. Upkeep: 6g/day

BAKERY.name: Bakery
BAKERY.description: Bakes bread from flour. Requires flour supply. Upkeep: 8g/day

FORGE.name: Forge
FORGE.description: A dedicated smithy. Forges tools or weapons from iron, or casts bronze ware from copper. Upkeep: 12g/day

TANNERY.name: Tannery
TANNERY.description: Tans animal hides into leather, leather armor or parchment. Upkeep: 8g/day

SAWMILL.name: Sawmill
SAWMILL.description: Processes timber into firewood and lumber. Upkeep: 7g/day

QUARRY.name: Quarry
QUARRY.description: Cuts stone blocks from rocky outcrops. Essential for construction. Upkeep: 8g/day

SALT_PANS.name: Salt Pans
SALT_PANS.description: Evaporates seawater to harvest salt. A vital food preservative. Upkeep: 6g/day

APIARY.name: Apiary
APIARY.description: Keeps beehives for honey. Used in mead and candle-making. Upkeep: 6g/day

ORCHARD.name: Orchard
ORCHARD.description: Cultivates fruit trees for winemaking or fresh trade. Upkeep: 6g/day

HEMP_FARM.name: Hemp Farm
HEMP_FARM.description: Grows hemp fiber for rope-making. Vital for ships and construction. Upkeep: 5g/day

CLAY_PIT.name: Clay Pit
CLAY_PIT.description: Digs raw clay from riverbeds. Used for pottery. Upkeep: 4g/day

DAIRY.name: Dairy
DAIRY.description: Raises dairy cattle to produce aged cheese. Popular with traders. Upkeep: 6g/day

SMOKEHOUSE.name: Smokehouse
SMOKEHOUSE.description: Smokes fish and cures meat for long-term preservation. Upkeep: 6g/day

BUTCHER.name: Butcher
BUTCHER.description: Processes hunted game and livestock into dried provisions. Upkeep: 5g/day

ROPE_WALK.name: Rope Walk
ROPE_WALK.description: Twists hemp fiber into rope. Vital for ships and construction. Upkeep: 5g/day

POTTERY_KILN.name: Pottery Kiln
POTTERY_KILN.description: Fires clay pots and vessels for households and traders. Upkeep: 5g/day

WEAVER.name: Weaver
WEAVER.description: Weaves wool into cloth and sews fine garments. Upkeep: 6g/day

WINERY.name: Winery
WINERY.description: Ferments fruit into wine and honey into mead. Premium beverages. Upkeep: 8g/day

APOTHECARY.name: Apothecary
APOTHECARY.description: Prepares herbal remedies and alchemical potions. Upkeep: 8g/day

FLETCHER.name: Fletcher
FLETCHER.description: Crafts arrows and bows for hunters and archers. Upkeep: 6g/day

JEWELER.name: Jeweler
JEWELER.description: Cuts gems and crafts fine jewelry for nobility. Upkeep: 10g/day

DYE_WORKS.name: Dye Works
DYE_WORKS.description: Extracts natural dyes from berries and plants. Upkeep: 6g/day

CHANDLERY.name: Chandlery
CHANDLERY.description: Renders beeswax into candles. An essential light source. Upkeep: 5g/day

GLASSWORKS.name: Glassworks
GLASSWORKS.description: Melts stone into glass and blows glass into lanterns. Upkeep: 10g/day

SCRIPTORIUM.name: Scriptorium
SCRIPTORIUM.description: Monks and scribes prepare parchment and copy rare texts. Upkeep: 8g/day

BLACKSMITH.name: Blacksmith
BLACKSMITH.description: Versatile smithy producing shields, tools, and weapons. Upkeep: 10g/day

PERFUMERY.name: Perfumery
PERFUMERY.description: Distils flowers and resins into perfumes and incense. Upkeep: 8g/day

HUNTING_LODGE.name: Hunting Lodge
HUNTING_LODGE.description: Hunters bring back hides for tanneries and scriptoriums. Upkeep: 5g/day

CATTLE_RANCH.name: Cattle Ranch
CATTLE_RANCH.description: Raises cattle for meat. Pair with a Smokehouse or Butcher for dried provisions. Built on or beside a cattle herd it yields 30% more. Upkeep: 6g/day

HERB_GARDEN.name: Herb Garden
HERB_GARDEN.description: Grows medicinal and aromatic herbs for apothecaries and perfumeries. Upkeep: 4g/day

HORSE_RANCH.name: Horse Ranch
HORSE_RANCH.description: Breeds horses — slow to raise but prized by every army and merchant. Upkeep: 12g/day

PITCH_WORKS.name: Pitch Works
PITCH_WORKS.description: Skims rock oil from a desert seep. Sell it, or refine it into lamp oil at a Chandlery. Upkeep: 8g/day

FORAGER_HUT.name: Forager's Hut
FORAGER_HUT.description: Gathers wild berries and mushrooms. Supplies Dye Works. Upkeep: 3g/day

GRAIN.name: Grain
GRAIN.description: Threshed wheat, barley or rye: what the farmers carry to the granary. Ground into flour, brewed into beer, or eaten as pottage in a lean year.

FLOUR.name: Flour
FLOUR.description: Grain ground at the mill. The baker turns it into bread; it keeps longer than the loaf.

BREAD.name: Bread
BREAD.description: Baked loaves, the staple of every table. Filling and cheap, but it goes stale within days.

FISH.name: Raw Fish
FISH.description: Fresh-caught fish. Eat it soon, grill it, or smoke it to make it keep.

PRESERVED_FISH.name: Smoked Fish
PRESERVED_FISH.description: Fish smoked or salted to keep for months: ships' stores, soldiers' rations and Lenten fare.

WOOD.name: Wood
WOOD.description: Felled timber. Burnt, sawn into planks, or worked by joiners, wheelwrights and shipwrights.

FIREWOOD.name: Firewood
FIREWOOD.description: Split logs for hearths and ovens. Every household burns it, most of all in winter.

WOOL.name: Wool
WOOL.description: Shorn fleece, washed and carded. Spun and woven into cloth, or felted into cloaks.

TEXTILES.name: Textiles
TEXTILES.description: Bolts of woven cloth, the tailor's stock. Most of the realm's clothes start here.

FLAX.name: Flax
FLAX.description: Retted and scutched flax from the fields, ready for the spinning wheel.

LINEN.name: Linen
LINEN.description: Linen cloth: shirts, shifts, sheets and altar cloths. Woven in town shops, or spun and woven in cottages for a merchant's piece rate.

CLOTHES.name: Clothes
CLOTHES.description: Plain made garments: tunics, hose and hoods. Clean clothes keep you presentable.

STONE.name: Stone
STONE.description: Quarried and dressed stone for walls, towers, bridges and the finer houses.

IRON.name: Iron
IRON.description: Bar iron from the bloomery. The smith's raw stuff for tools, nails and blades.

TOOLS.name: Tools
TOOLS.description: Axes, saws, hammers and ploughshares. Workshops and farms use them up and need more.

WEAPONS.name: Weapons
WEAPONS.description: Munition swords, axes and spearheads from the armourer, by the dozen. Armies and town watches buy them in war, and every recruit wants one.

GOLD_ORE.name: Gold Ore
GOLD_ORE.description: Gold-bearing rock from the mines, to be smelted into bars.

COPPER.name: Copper
COPPER.description: Smelted copper from the hill mines. The founders cast it into bronze; tinkers and coppersmiths use the rest.

BRONZE.name: Bronze Ware
BRONZE.description: Pots, bells, lamps, buckles and ship's fittings, cast from the copper of these hills (its own arsenic hardens it: no tin needed).

IRON_INGOT.name: Iron Ingot
IRON_INGOT.description: Refined iron cast in ingots, cleaner than bar iron: wanted for good steel and fine work.

GOLD_BAR.name: Gold Bar
GOLD_BAR.description: Smelted gold. Mints strike it into coin; goldsmiths make it into jewellery.

SILVER_ORE.name: Silver Ore
SILVER_ORE.description: Argentiferous ore from the hill mines. Silversmiths work a little of it; the realms' mints buy the rest and strike it into coin.

GEMS.name: Gems
GEMS.description: Cut and uncut stones: rubies, garnets, amethysts. Small, light and very valuable.

IVORY.name: Ivory
IVORY.description: Tusk ivory from distant lands, carved into combs, caskets and chess pieces for the rich.

SPICES.name: Spices
SPICES.description: Pepper, cumin and cinnamon from the trade routes. A little goes a long way in a lord's kitchen.

HORSES.name: Horses
HORSES.description: A string of horses for sale or trade: farm horses, pack animals and remounts.

BEER.name: Beer
BEER.description: Ale brewed from grain. Safer than water, and drunk by everyone, morning to night.

LIQUOR.name: Liquor
LIQUOR.description: Distilled spirits. Strong, costly, and quick to start a brawl.

LUXURIES.name: Luxuries
LUXURIES.description: Fine goods for great households: glass, silver plate, carpets and the like.

SMALL_FISH.name: Small Fry
SMALL_FISH.description: Small fry from the shallows. Cheap food, or bait for bigger catches.

LARGE_FISH.name: Large Cod
LARGE_FISH.description: A big cod, enough for a family supper. Sells well fresh, better smoked.

CRAB.name: Crab
CRAB.description: A live crab from the rocks. Boiled, it fetches a fair price at a coastal market.

SWORDFISH.name: Swordfish
SWORDFISH.description: A deep-water fighter, hard to land and prized at any fishmonger's.

LOBSTER.name: Lobster
LOBSTER.description: A lobster from the pots, a delicacy on noble tables.

GOLDEN_FISH.name: Golden Fish
GOLDEN_FISH.description: A rare golden fish. Collectors and lords pay far more than its weight in silver.

BOOT.name: Old Boot
BOOT.description: An old boot pulled from the water. Worth nothing, but it proves you were fishing.

SEAWEED.name: Seaweed
SEAWEED.description: Wrack from the shore: spread on fields as manure, burnt for potash, or eaten in a hard winter.

MUSSELS.name: Mussels
MUSSELS.description: Blue-black mussels prised off the rocks and the river bed. Steamed, a cheap and filling supper.

OYSTERS.name: Oysters
OYSTERS.description: Oysters brought up from the sea floor. Eaten raw at a lord's table, and now and then one holds a pearl.

CRAYFISH.name: Crayfish
CRAYFISH.description: Freshwater crayfish caught by hand under the stones of a river or lake. Boiled, they make a fair meal.

SEA_SPONGE.name: Sea Sponge
SEA_SPONGE.description: A soft sponge cut from the deep rocks. Bathhouses, physicians and scribes pay for it.

ORE.name: Iron Ore
ORE.description: Iron-bearing rock from the mines. Smelted in a bloomery with coal or charcoal it gives bar iron.

HERBS.name: Herbs
HERBS.description: Gathered wild herbs for physicians, apothecaries and the cooking pot.

PELTS.name: Pelts
PELTS.description: Furs from the hunt: fox, beaver, marten. Furriers make them into trims and coats.

BERRIES.name: Berries
BERRIES.description: Wild berries picked from the hedgerows. A handful staves off hunger; they spoil fast.

MUSHROOMS.name: Mushrooms
MUSHROOMS.description: Forest mushrooms. Good eating, if whoever picked them knew which ones.

MEAT.name: Meat
MEAT.description: Fresh meat from the hunt or the butcher. Cook it, or dry it before it turns.

HIDE.name: Hide
HIDE.description: A raw animal skin. The tannery turns it into leather.

LEATHER.name: Leather
LEATHER.description: Tanned hide. Townsfolk wear it out as boots, belts and harness; tanneries make it from hides.

ANTLER.name: Antler
ANTLER.description: Shed or taken antler, carved into handles, combs and buttons.

FEATHER.name: Feather
FEATHER.description: Flight feathers, for fletching arrows and for quills.

HORSE.name: Horse
HORSE.description: A riding horse: faster travel on the world map, and more room in your packs.

AGRI_PARTS.name: Agricultural Implements
AGRI_PARTS.description: Ploughs, harrows and mill gear. Raise the yield of farms that use them.

INDUSTRY_PARTS.name: Industrial Components
INDUSTRY_PARTS.description: Bellows, gears and fittings for forges, mills and workshops.

MILITARY_PARTS.name: Military Supplies
MILITARY_PARTS.description: Arms, harness and camp gear for raising and keeping troops.

INFRA_PARTS.name: Engineering Plans
INFRA_PARTS.description: Surveys and engineers' drawings for roads, bridges and public works.

COMMERCE_PARTS.name: Trade Documents
COMMERCE_PARTS.description: Contracts, bills and charters: the paperwork trade houses run on.

EXOTIC_SPICES.name: Exotic Spices
EXOTIC_SPICES.description: Saffron, cloves and nutmeg from the far edge of the trade routes. Worth their weight in silver.

SILK.name: Silk Cloth
SILK.description: Silk cloth from distant looms. Only the rich wear it.

PERFUME.name: Perfume
PERFUME.description: Scents in small glass vials, a gift that wins favour at court.

TEA.name: Tea Leaves
TEA.description: Dried tea leaves, a costly import that a few great houses have taken to.

WINE.name: Fine Wine
WINE.description: Good wine in casks, served at feasts and given as gifts between lords.

CHEESE.name: Aged Cheese
CHEESE.description: Aged hard cheese. Keeps for months and travels well.

MILK.name: Milk
MILK.description: Fresh milk from your cows and goats. Drink it, or sell it in town before it turns.

EGGS.name: Eggs
EGGS.description: Eggs from your hens and ducks. Cheap, filling, and every kitchen wants them.

DRIED_MEAT.name: Dried Meat
DRIED_MEAT.description: Salted and dried meat. Light and lasting: soldiers' and travellers' food.

HONEY.name: Honey
HONEY.description: Honey from the hives: sweetener, preserver, and the makings of mead.

SALT.name: Salt
SALT.description: Salt from pans or mines. Without it no meat or fish keeps through the winter.

ROPE.name: Rope
ROPE.description: Hemp rope for ships, wells, cranes and farms.

CANDLES.name: Candles
CANDLES.description: Tallow candles for light after dark. Beeswax ones go to churches and the rich.

POTTERY.name: Pottery
POTTERY.description: Fired pots, jugs and bowls for every kitchen and storeroom.

LEATHER_ARMOR.name: Leather Armour
LEATHER_ARMOR.description: A boiled-leather jerkin. Light, quiet and cheap; it turns a glancing blow.

SHIELD.name: Round Shield
SHIELD.description: Glued boards faced with rawhide, an iron boss over the grip: the common soldier's shield.

BOW.name: Bow
BOW.description: A hunting or war bow of yew or ash. Useless without arrows.

ARROWS.name: Arrows
ARROWS.description: Fletched arrows, sold by the each: every shot at game uses one, and a hunter gets some back.

BOLTS.name: Crossbow Bolts
BOLTS.description: Short, heavy iron-headed bolts for the crossbow, sold by the each. Crossbowmen spend them in every battle; a crossbow hunter uses them on game.

FISHING_SPEAR.name: Fishing Spear
FISHING_SPEAR.description: A light barbed spear for taking fish underwater. It wears with use.

SINEW.name: Sinew
SINEW.description: Dried tendon from a butchered beast: twisted into bowstrings and lashings.

CURED_FURS.name: Cured Furs
CURED_FURS.description: Fleshed, salted and stretched pelts, ready for the furrier.

BEAR_RUG.name: Bear-skin Rug
BEAR_RUG.description: A cured bear's pelt, head and all, to lie before a lord's hearth.

LEATHER_GOODS.name: Leather Goods
LEATHER_GOODS.description: Belts, pouches, purses and straps: every traveller wants one.

CARVINGS.name: Carvings
CARVINGS.description: Whittled spoons, bowls, toys and antler combs.

IVORY_CARVING.name: Ivory Carving
IVORY_CARVING.description: A figure or casket panel carved in ivory, for the luxury trade.

QUILLS.name: Quills
QUILLS.description: Cut and hardened feather pens. Scribes, clerks and monasteries buy them.

HEALING_SALVE.name: Healing Salve
HEALING_SALVE.description: An ointment of herbs and fat that cleans and closes wounds.

POTION.name: Strange Potion
POTION.description: A murky brew from a hedge-witch. Nobody quite knows what it does.

ELIXIR.name: Elixir of Vigor
ELIXIR.description: An apothecary's tonic that restores strength and wards off fatigue.

ANTIDOTE.name: Antidote
ANTIDOTE.description: A remedy against poisons and the bites of venomous beasts.

TREASURE_MAP.name: Treasure Map
TREASURE_MAP.description: A weathered map marking something buried. It may be real.

ANCIENT_COIN.name: Ancient Coin
ANCIENT_COIN.description: A coin from a fallen empire. Collectors and scholars pay well for it.

RARE_BOOK.name: Rare Book
RARE_BOOK.description: A precious manuscript. Scholars, monasteries and libraries want it.

COMPASS.name: Compass
COMPASS.description: A lodestone needle in a brass case. Sailors and explorers swear by it.

LANTERN.name: Lantern
LANTERN.description: A horn-paned lantern that lights the road at night and keeps the flame out of the wind.

AMULET.name: Amulet
AMULET.description: A charm said to ward off ill luck. Some believe in it more than others.

ENCHANTED_RING.name: Enchanted Ring
ENCHANTED_RING.description: A ring with a strange glimmer. Its owner swears it brings fortune.

DYES.name: Dyes
DYES.description: Woad, madder and weld: the colours that make cloth worth more.

INCENSE.name: Incense
INCENSE.description: Fragrant resins burnt in temples and in the chambers of the wealthy.

HEMP.name: Hemp Fiber
HEMP.description: Hemp fibre, twisted into rope and woven into sacking and sailcloth.

CLAY.name: Raw Clay
CLAY.description: Dug clay for the potter's wheel and the brick kiln.

FRUIT.name: Fresh Fruit
FRUIT.description: Apples, pears and plums fresh from the orchard. Eat them, or press them for cider.

VEGETABLES.name: Vegetables
VEGETABLES.description: Cabbages, turnips and carrots from a kitchen garden. Plain fare that fills a pot.

WHEAT_SEED.name: Seed Wheat
WHEAT_SEED.description: A measure of seed corn: sow it on tilled ground in spring or summer (data/crops.json).

CABBAGE_SEED.name: Cabbage Seed
CABBAGE_SEED.description: Sow on tilled ground from spring to autumn. Hardy: cabbages stand the winter frost.

TURNIP_SEED.name: Turnip Seed
TURNIP_SEED.description: Quick to come up. Sow on tilled ground in spring or autumn; hardy through the frosts.

CARROT_SEED.name: Carrot Seed
CARROT_SEED.description: Sow on tilled ground in spring or summer.

FLAX_SEED.name: Linseed
FLAX_SEED.description: Flax seed for the spring sowing. The crop is pulled for the spinners.

HEMP_SEED.name: Hemp Seed
HEMP_SEED.description: Sow on tilled ground in spring or summer; it grows tall and wants little water.

HERB_SEED.name: Herb Seed
HERB_SEED.description: Seed for a herb bed. Sow in spring or summer.

STRAWBERRY_SEED.name: Strawberry Runners
STRAWBERRY_SEED.description: Runners for a strawberry bed. Sow in spring or summer and keep them well watered.

GLASS.name: Glass
GLASS.description: Blown and cast glass for windows, bottles and lamps.

MEAD.name: Mead
MEAD.description: Honey wine, sweet and strong, an old drink of the halls.

PARCHMENT.name: Parchment
PARCHMENT.description: Scraped and stretched skin to write on: letters, charters and books.

FOOD.name: Army Rations
FOOD.description: Hardtack and salt pork seized from soldiers. Eaten on the road like any other food.

COAL.name: Coal
COAL.description: Mined from coal seams. Smiths and smelters burn it: forges near coal work faster, and a furnace makes ingots from less iron with it.

OIL.name: Rock Oil
OIL.description: Black oil from desert seeps. A prized trade good; chandlers refine it into lamp oil.

LAMP_OIL.name: Lamp Oil
LAMP_OIL.description: Refined oil for lamps and lanterns.

RUM.name: Rum
RUM.description: Pirate rum. A swig puts spring back in your step (+1 movement today).

HOLY_WATER.name: Holy Water
HOLY_WATER.description: Blessed water carried by pilgrims. Drink it to mend small wounds (+10 health).

RELICS.name: Holy Relics
RELICS.description: Bones and tokens of saints. A pious lord treasures them; a House that enshrines them gains standing.

SCRIPTURES.name: Scriptures
SCRIPTURES.description: Illuminated holy texts. A modest courtly gift.

POISON.name: Poison
POISON.description: Smuggled poison. Fences pay well and ask nothing.

FORGED_DOCUMENTS.name: Forged Documents
FORGED_DOCUMENTS.description: Passable letters of introduction. Carrying them helps a little at the negotiating table (+2%).

RARE_HERBS.name: Rare Herbs
RARE_HERBS.description: Exotic herbs. An apothecary brews them into an Elixir of Vigor.

ANCIENT_ARTIFACT.name: Ancient Artifact
ANCIENT_ARTIFACT.description: A relic of a lost age from a creature's hoard. Lords covet it; enshrined in your hall it brings your House prestige.

ENCHANTED_WEAPON.name: Enchanted Weapon
ENCHANTED_WEAPON.description: A rune-etched blade from a legendary hoard. Carried at the head of your army it adds 5% battle power.

DRAGON_SCALE.name: Dragon Scale
DRAGON_SCALE.description: A plate of scale harder than steel. Carried as a buckler it turns 10% of the harm you take; a blacksmith can work three into dragonscale armour.

DRAGONSCALE_ARMOR.name: Dragonscale Armour
DRAGONSCALE_ARMOR.description: Armour of dragon scale. Turns 25% of the harm you take, and kings would trade a province for it.

ROYAL_SEAL.name: Royal Seal
ROYAL_SEAL.description: A sovereign's signet. Carrying it lends you authority in negotiation (+5%); returned to a lord it earns real gratitude.

TREATY.name: Sealed Treaty
TREATY.description: Signed terms between courts. Useful leverage at the table (+3% negotiation), or a gift a lord will value.

GIFT_CHEST.name: Gift Chest
GIFT_CHEST.description: A chest of courtly presents meant for a lord. Present it at a royal audience.

FINE_WINE.name: Fine Wine
FINE_WINE.description: A vintage fit for a royal table. A small courtly gift.

CURSED_IDOL.name: Cursed Idol
CURSED_IDOL.description: A grinning idol carried up out of a delve. While you carry it the curse saps a little health and karma each day and dogs your luck below ground. Sell it or be rid of it some other way.

RESIN.name: Pine Resin
RESIN.description: Sticky resin tapped from pines: incense, ink and pitch.

TALLOW.name: Tallow
TALLOW.description: Rendered animal fat, for candles and soap.

PLANKS.name: Sawn Planks
PLANKS.description: Timber sawn to boards: the joiner's and cooper's stock.

STEEL.name: Steel
STEEL.description: Iron worked with charcoal into hard steel: the best blades, tools and plate.

SILVER_BAR.name: Silver Bar
SILVER_BAR.description: Refined silver, cast for the silversmith.

INK.name: Ink
INK.description: Soot and resin ground into a black ink.

JOINERY.name: Joinery
JOINERY.description: Stools, chests and tables: a joiner's honest work.

BARREL.name: Barrel
BARREL.description: An iron-hooped oak barrel, wanted by every brewer and fishmonger.

GRAVE_CROSS.name: Grave Cross
GRAVE_CROSS.description: A wooden cross cut and pegged by the grave carver, to set at the head of a grave.

HEADSTONE.name: Headstone
HEADSTONE.description: A dressed stone slab from the mason's yard, cut with a name: a grave that is remembered.

CARVED_HEADSTONE.name: Carved Headstone
CARVED_HEADSTONE.description: A tall headstone carved with a border and a verse by a master mason: the gentry's grave.

CHAINMAIL.name: Mail Hauberk
CHAINMAIL.description: A knee-length shirt of riveted iron rings over a padded coat. Turns a cut; a mace or a point still bruises through.

PLATE_ARMOR.name: Plate Harness
PLATE_ARMOR.description: Fitted steel plate from head to foot: a knight's harness. Heavy, and worth it.

HELMET.name: Iron Helm
HELMET.description: A conical iron helm with a nasal.

STEEL_SWORD.name: Steel Longsword
STEEL_SWORD.description: A long tempered steel blade, better balanced than any munition sword: the knight's sword.

SPEAR.name: Iron Spear
SPEAR.description: An ash shaft and an iron head: the commoner's weapon.

CROSSBOW.name: Crossbow
CROSSBOW.description: A stocked bow with an iron lath and a cranked string.

STEEL_TOOLS.name: Steel Tools
STEEL_TOOLS.description: Steel-edged chisels, saws and hammers: a craftsman works faster and finer with them.

SADDLE.name: Saddle
SADDLE.description: A leather riding saddle with iron fittings.

WOOL_CLOAK.name: Wool Cloak
WOOL_CLOAK.description: A heavy woollen cloak against the wind and rain.

FUR_COAT.name: Fur Coat
FUR_COAT.description: Pelts sewn over wool: proof against a northern winter.

FINE_GARMENTS.name: Fine Garments
FINE_GARMENTS.description: Dyed silk and linen cut for the court.

MEAT_PIE.name: Meat Pie
MEAT_PIE.description: Pastry and meat: a meal you can carry.

SAUSAGE.name: Sausage
SAUSAGE.description: Salted meat in a skin: keeps for weeks.

JAM.name: Fruit Preserve
JAM.description: Fruit boiled down with honey and sealed in a crock.

PICKLES.name: Pickled Vegetables
PICKLES.description: Vegetables put up in brine for the winter.

SOAP.name: Soap
SOAP.description: Tallow and wood-ash lye. Washing with it gets you and your clothes cleaner.

GOLD_JEWELLERY.name: Gold Jewellery
GOLD_JEWELLERY.description: Gold set with gems: jewellery for a lord.

POULTICE.name: Poultice
POULTICE.description: Herbs bound in linen against a wound.

TONIC.name: Herbal Tonic
TONIC.description: Herbs steeped in honeyed wine: heals and revives.

BOOK.name: Bound Book
BOOK.description: Parchment leaves, inked and bound in leather.

TIN.name: Tin
TIN.description: Tin from the stream-works and the far mines: a quarter part of it turns soft copper into hard bronze.

BRONZE_BAR.name: Bronze Bar
BRONZE_BAR.description: Copper and tin cast in bars: the bronzesmith's stuff for blades, axes and spearheads.

HAFT.name: Ash Haft
HAFT.description: A straight ash shaft for a spear, an axe, a mace or a polearm.

GRIP.name: Hilt & Grip
GRIP.description: A leather-bound grip with guard and pommel, ready to take a blade.

SHIELD_BOSS.name: Shield Boss
SHIELD_BOSS.description: A domed iron boss that covers a shield's grip.

WHETSTONE.name: Whetstone
WHETSTONE.description: A fine-grained stone for keeping an edge on a blade. It cracks in time.

RONDEL_DAGGER.name: Steel Rondel Dagger
RONDEL_DAGGER.description: A stiff steel spike between two discs: it finds the gaps in mail and plate.

BRONZE_SWORD.name: Bronze Leaf Sword
BRONZE_SWORD.description: A cast bronze leaf blade: old-fashioned, and it bends.

IRON_SWORD.name: Iron Arming Sword
IRON_SWORD.description: A one-handed iron sword for sword and shield.

STEEL_ARMING_SWORD.name: Steel Arming Sword
STEEL_ARMING_SWORD.description: A steel-edged one-handed sword, quick and keen.

BRONZE_AXE.name: Bronze Axe
BRONZE_AXE.description: A cast bronze axe head on an ash haft.

IRON_AXE.name: Bearded War Axe
IRON_AXE.description: A light bearded axe: it hooks shields and bites through mail rings.

DANE_AXE.name: Steel Dane Axe
DANE_AXE.description: A broad axe on a five-foot haft: two hands, terrible blows.

IRON_MACE.name: Iron Mace
IRON_MACE.description: A heavy iron mace: it crushes through mail.

FLANGED_MACE.name: Steel Flanged Mace
FLANGED_MACE.description: A flanged steel mace made for beating plate.

BRONZE_SPEAR.name: Bronze Spear
BRONZE_SPEAR.description: A bronze spearhead on an ash haft.

PIKE.name: Pike
PIKE.description: A long shaft with a small iron head: two hands, and a wall of them stops horse.

IRON_BILL.name: Bill
IRON_BILL.description: A hooked blade, spike and back-hook on a long haft: the yeoman's polearm.

HALBERD.name: Steel Halberd
HALBERD.description: Axe, spike and hook in one steel head on a long haft.

BUCKLER.name: Buckler
BUCKLER.description: A small iron fist-shield: quick to parry and riposte, little cover.

HEATER_SHIELD.name: Heater Shield
HEATER_SHIELD.description: A leather-faced, iron-rimmed shield in the knightly shape.

KITE_SHIELD.name: Kite Shield
KITE_SHIELD.description: A long shield from shoulder to shin.

PAVISE.name: Pavise
PAVISE.description: A tall standing shield to reload behind.

STEEL_HELM.name: Steel Bascinet
STEEL_HELM.description: A close steel helm with a padded lining.

GAMBESON.name: Gambeson
GAMBESON.description: A quilted coat of cloth and wool: the poor man's armour, and worn under mail.

BRIGANDINE.name: Brigandine
BRIGANDINE.description: Steel plates riveted inside a cloth coat.

LINEN.name: Weave Linen
LINEN.description: Spin flax and weave it into linen.

CAST_BRONZE.name: Cast Bronze
CAST_BRONZE.description: Melt copper (its own arsenic hardens it) and cast pots, bells and fittings.

BEER.name: Brew Beer
BEER.description: Brew ale from grain. Popular at taverns.

LIQUOR.name: Distill Liquor
LIQUOR.description: Distill strong spirits from grain. High value.

LEATHER_ARMOR.name: Tan Leather Armor
LEATHER_ARMOR.description: Cure hides into protective leather armor.

DRIED_MEAT.name: Cure Dried Meat
DRIED_MEAT.description: Cure raw meat into dried provisions.

POTTERY.name: Fire Pottery
POTTERY.description: Fire clay into pots and vessels.

TAN_LEATHER.name: Tan Leather
TAN_LEATHER.description: Cure hides into leather for the town's cobblers and saddlers.

SHIELD.name: Forge Shield
SHIELD.description: Hammer iron into a sturdy shield.

ARROWS.name: Fletch Arrows
ARROWS.description: Whittle and tip arrows for archers.

BOW.name: Craft Bow
BOW.description: Bend a yew stave into a longbow.

HEALING_SALVE.name: Brew Healing Salve
HEALING_SALVE.description: Infuse herbs into a medicinal salve.

POTION.name: Brew Potion
POTION.description: Brew mushrooms into a mysterious potion.

IRON_INGOT.name: Smelt Iron Ingots
IRON_INGOT.description: Smelt iron into ingots. Coal nearby fires the furnace hotter.

DRAGONSCALE_ARMOR.name: Forge Dragonscale Armour
DRAGONSCALE_ARMOR.description: Rivet dragon scales into a suit of armour.

LAMP_OIL.name: Refine Lamp Oil
LAMP_OIL.description: Refine rock oil into clean-burning lamp oil.

ELIXIR.name: Brew Elixir of Vigor
ELIXIR.description: Brew rare herbs into a restorative elixir.
